input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: Reusing the wrapper's statistics dictionary removes per-call isolation for recursive and overlapping calls. The same change in the async wrapper also lets concurrent tasks overwrite each other's retry statistics.
- rationale: When a retry-decorated function recursively calls itself, the inner invocation clears the dictionary still used by the outer invocation and assigns it to its own retry controller. If the inner call takes three attempts while the outer succeeds on its first attempt, the outer call's final statistics incorrectly report three attempts. Concurrent async calls likewise clear and update the same dictionary, producing statistics that mix separate calls; previously each copy had its own dictionary.
critique: The finding points to the same mechanism as the label: one statistics dict is reused across calls. Overlapping, recursive or concurrent async calls then clear and overwrite each other's stats, which produces mixed or wrong statistics. This covers the label's concurrent/nested failure path.
